The green methanol market is witnessing steady growth, driven by a rising focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and addressing climate change, which is increasing the demand for green methanol as a sustainable alternative to traditional fossil fuel-derived methanol. Additionally, government policies that promote renewable energy usage and aim to decrease greenhouse gas emissions are further fueling investment and expansion in the green methanol market.
The green methanol market comprises biomass, green hydrogen, and carbon capture & storage. The carbon capture & storage segment is expected to grow at the highest rate during the forecast period due to its ability to reduce CO2 emissions, making production more sustainable. This attracts industries aiming to lower their carbon footprints and comply with environmental regulations.
The key derivatives include formaldehyde, gasoline, green methanol-to-olefins/ green methanol-to-propylene, methyl tert-butyl ether, acetic acid, dimethyl ether, methyl methacrylate, biodiesel, and others. The demand for green methanol-to-olefin has been growing rapidly. Methyl tert-butyl ether, a gasoline additive that enhances air quality, and dimethyl ether, a clean-burning fuel with properties like propane, highlight green methanol's versatility.
The application segment includes chemical feedstock, fuel, and others. The fuel segment is expected to register the highest CAGR in the market due to its increasing adoption in marine and sustainable aviation fuels. Green methanol's low carbon footprint and compatibility with existing infrastructure make it an attractive choice for reducing emissions in the marine industry.
Green methanol market covers Europe, North America, Asia Pacific, South America and Middle East and Africa. North America leads the green methanol market due to the high demand for sustainable fuels, supportive government policies, the presence of key industry players, abundant renewable feedstock, and significant investments in infrastructure and technology.
The major market players have adopted both organic and inorganic strategies including new product launches, acquisitions, partnerships, and expansions. For instance, in February 2025, Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company Methanol Reformer S.L. and Element Corp. signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to collaborate on developing and commercializing hydrogen solutions using methanol reforming technology, focusing on the design, manufacture, and sales of modular, mass-producible Methanol-to-Hydrogen generators.

This growth is primarily driven by the increasing emphasis on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and mitigating climate change, which is accelerating demand for green methanol as a more sustainable alternative to conventionally produced, fossil fuel-based methanol. Furthermore, supportive government policies promoting renewable energy adoption and emissions reduction are encouraging investments and driving the expansion of the green methanol market.
From 2026 to 2032, the biomass segment will be the largest, by volume, in the green methanol market.
The biomass segment is emerging as a significant and rapidly expanding component of the green methanol industry, utilizing a diverse range of organic feedstocks, including agricultural residues, forestry waste, and municipal solid waste. As a renewable and widely available resource, biomass can be replenished continuously, supporting a consistent feedstock supply for methanol production. In addition, government incentives and supportive policies promoting the utilization of renewable resources are enhancing the economic viability of biomass-based methanol production. Compared with certain other renewable pathways, such as hydrogen produced through electrolysis, biomass can offer a more cost-competitive feedstock option, particularly in regions with abundant biomass resources and established waste-collection infrastructure.
By application, the fuel segment will be the fastest growing in the green methanol market from 2026 to 2032.
The transportation sector, particularly maritime shipping, is increasingly seeking low-carbon fuel alternatives to meet stringent emissions regulations and decarbonization targets. Green methanol is emerging as a viable sustainable alternative to conventional fossil-based fuels due to its potential to reduce lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions. The International Maritime Organization (IMO) has introduced increasingly stringent measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from shipping, supporting growing interest in methanol as a marine fuel. In parallel, government incentives, subsidies, and supportive policies for low-carbon fuels are encouraging the adoption of green methanol across transportation applications, including marine vessels and other heavy-duty mobility segments. As a result, green methanol is gaining prominence as a potential fuel in the transition to a lower-carbon, more sustainable transportation and energy system.

North America leads the green methanol market.
North America is expected to lead the green methanol market in terms of CAGR, supported by favorable regulatory frameworks, including Canada's Clean Fuel Standard and the US Renewable Fuel Standard. Technological advancements, such as Carbon Clean Solutions' MTJet technology for sustainable aviation fuel production, together with strategic collaborations involving companies such as Methanex and Gevo, are further supporting market development. Government funding and incentives, coupled with increasing adoption of green methanol across the maritime and aviation sectors, are accelerating the region's transition toward sustainable fuels. In addition, growing investments in carbon capture and utilization (CCU) technologies and the integration of green methanol with hybrid-electric systems are expanding its potential across multiple end-use industries, strengthening North America's position in the global green methanol market.

Capital is flowing into green methanol, but through a different mechanism than in more mature industrial sectors: mega-scale project financings and offtake-backed construction decisions dominate, with outright company M&A still thin. The global green methanol market was valued at USD 2.59 billion in 2025 and is expected to grow to USD 3.46 billion in 2026, roughly 31% year-over-year, reaching USD 20.11 billion by 2032 at a 34.1% CAGR on this estimate.
The market is also splitting along production pathway. By product, bio-methanol holds the largest 2025 market value at USD 1.7 billion, as companies keep exploring renewable feedstock from waste and biomass, while e-methanol development advances as renewable electricity access improves, enabling chemical production through electrolysis and carbon capture. The one deal of real scale reshaped the competitive map: in September 2024, Methanex Corporation entered a definitive agreement to acquire OCI Global's international methanol business for USD 2.05 billion, a purchase price implying a multiple of 7.5 times adjusted EBITDA at a $350/MT realized methanol price and completed the acquisition on June 27, 2025.
